ISOLATED GIT WORKTREE of /workspace/SuperGrok1.5, branched from the FULL state (3 flagships + full TP for all 3 models + resource planner + EP + size-adaptive + memory-strategy + datasets + host bring-up). Freely Edit/Write/Bash/build/run.
PROCEDURE: read the cited code/specs IN FULL; implement; build+gate; restore dirty *.pyc (git checkout -- on pyc), git add -A, git commit -m "finish: <area>"; report git rev-parse HEAD. Be HONEST in gate_pass.
RULES: keep the SingleGPU/default path byte-identical (the 3 model pytests are the byte-identity gates); gfx942/tpu untouched. NVSHMEM_HOME=/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/nvidia/nvshmem. scripts/compile_to_object.sh at repo root.

GOAL: enable the ACTUAL cross-GPU one-model-across-8 run (the capability track). The kernel+launcher already compile under ParTP8+NvshmemTransport RDC; the missing piece is the host NVSHMEM bring-up, which canNOT be driven from Python (no nvshmem python binding). Add a small C++ pybind (a new TU, or extend the launcher build) exposing: nvshmem_init via the UID bootstrap (nvshmemx_get_uniqueid + nvshmemx_init_attr with the UID broadcast over torch.distributed/NCCL — MPI/PMI are absent; the UID plugin nvshmem_bootstrap_uid IS present), nvshmem_team_split_strided for the TP team, and the collective nvshmem_malloc of the symmetric tp_sym_heap (matching dec_tc_ensure_tp_sym_heap). Wire it into tuning/flagship_distributed.py (the harness has the dry-run + TPBootstrapBlocked stub — replace the stub with the real pybind call). Then a 2-GPU SMOKE: torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 a minimal nvshmem_init+team+malloc+a tiny all-reduce, asserting cross-rank correctness. BE HONEST: if the multi-GPU torchrun+NVSHMEM bring-up hits a runpod/container blocker, deliver the apply-ready pybind + the smoke script + scope the exact blocker (this is the genuine wildcard). gate: the 2-GPU nvshmem smoke runs OR the blocker is precisely scoped. area=nvshmem_pybind.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

16	  * Mesh = TP8 x DP1 x PP1 + ZeRO-3 (the recommended config; see flagship_budget.py §0).
17	    Other meshes are selectable but the budget gate refuses an OOM config LOUDLY.

21	    build, exactly like decoder_bench.py — no setup.py change, no 33/33-gate impact).
22	  * It does not re-implement the fused step: the cross-rank DP path reuses the proven
23	    grokking_optimizers.parallel.distributed_step / zero3 modules; the TP all-reduce is
24	    IN-KERNEL (tp_transport.cuh), kept inside the one megakernel launch.
25	
26	USAGE
27	  python tuning/flagship_distributed.py --help                     # per-rank budget table
28	  python tuning/flagship_distributed.py --dry-run --model decoder --gpus 8  # CPU plan proof
29	  torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 tuning/flagship_distributed.py --steps 2 --dry-run
30	  torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 tuning/flagship_distributed.py --opt supergrok2 --steps 50
31	  torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 tuning/flagship_distributed.py --bench-all --steps 200
32	
33	DRY-RUN CONTRACT (the cheap gate, no GPU/NVSHMEM): validates the full 4D mesh, the TP
34	Megatron weight-shard (per-rank Nmax = kDecMaxTensorNumel/TP), the symmetric-heap stride
35	+ tp_comm_handle encoding, and the per-rank HBM budget for EVERY rank — on CPU — so the
36	operator SEES the fit + bring-up proof before spending GPU-hours on the (large) flagship
37	compile. The single-process `--gpus 8` form validates all 8 ranks; the torchrun form
38	validates this rank.
39	
40	REAL DATA (north star): grokking_race_v2.make_data_for_task (the modular-arithmetic
41	grokking task: tokens [B,seq=4] int32, targets [B] int32, vocab p=99) — the same pipeline
42	the production race uses; identical across ranks (seeded), TP-replicated batch.
43	"""
44	from __future__ import annotations
45	
46	import argparse
47	import math
48	import os
49	import sys
50	from pathlib import Path
51	
52	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
53	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
54	
55	from grokking_optimizers.parallel import flagship_budget as fb  # noqa: E402
56	from grokking_optimizers.distributed import (  # noqa: E402
57	    ParallelConfig,
58	    partition_tensor_parallel,
59	    TPBootstrap,
60	    bootstrap_tp_team,
61	)
62	from grokking_optimizers.host_bringup import (  # noqa: E402
63	    nvshmem_available,
64	    find_nvshmem_host_lib,
65	    TPBootstrapBlocked,
66	    decode_tp_comm_handle,
67	)
68	
69	_TC_TU = str(ROOT / "csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu")
70	_FLAGSHIP_LAYOUT = "csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_flagship_layout.cuh"
71	
72	
73	# ───────────────────────── flagship named-sizes (host TP shard input) ─────────
74	# The decoder's named_parameters() order + per-tensor 2D shapes (so the Megatron
75	# col/row split knows WHICH dim to divide). Built from the flagship dims WITHOUT
76	# importing torch or the kernel (pure shapes), so the dry-run validates the TP shard
77	# on CPU. This mirrors decoder_flagship_layout.cuh's kSizes ordering: per layer
78	# [in_proj 3d×d, out_proj d×d, ff.0 4d×d, ff.2 d×4d] + the norms/biases, plus the
79	# embeddings + final unembed. The shard math only needs the SPLIT tensors' shapes to
80	# be exact; the replicated remainder is summed as a single "replicated" bucket so the
81	# total matches kDecTotalElems.
82	
83	def flagship_named_shapes():
84	    """[(name, (out,in) | (numel,))] for the flagship decoder, named_parameters()
85	    order, faithful to decoder_flagship_layout.cuh's kSizes histogram so the TP shard's
86	    per-rank Nmax matches the real kernel (kDecMaxTensorNumel/TP, NOT an artifact of
87	    lumping the replicated tensors). The four large per-layer matrices carry their 2D
88	    shape (the Megatron col/row split needs it to pick the split dim); the replicated
89	    tensors (embeddings/unembed/norms/biases) are emitted INDIVIDUALLY (their real
90	    sizes), so the largest replicated tensor is the embedding (158,400 = vocab*d-ish),
91	    far below a per-rank split shard (10.24M/8 = 1.28M). Grand total == kDecTotalElems.
92	
93	    REAL replicated histogram (decoder_flagship_layout.cuh kSizes): {158400:2, 6400:49,
94	    4800:48, 1600:290, 99:1} (sum 1,324,899). We reproduce it EXACTLY so the per-rank
95	    resident-params and Nmax are the live numbers, not estimates."""
96	    d, dff, L = fb.FLAGSHIP_D, fb.FLAGSHIP_DFF, fb.FLAGSHIP_LAYERS
97	    shapes = []
98	    split_total = 0
99	    for li in range(L):
100	        # attention: in_proj (QKV, column-parallel) 3d×d ; out_proj (row-parallel) d×d
101	        shapes.append((f"layers.{li}.attn.in_proj.weight", (3 * d, d)))
102	        shapes.append((f"layers.{li}.attn.out_proj.weight", (d, d)))
103	        # mlp: ff.0 (column-parallel) 4d×d ; ff.2 (row-parallel) d×4d
104	        shapes.append((f"layers.{li}.mlp.ff.0.weight", (dff, d)))
105	        shapes.append((f"layers.{li}.mlp.ff.2.weight", (d, dff)))
106	        split_total += (3 * d * d) + (d * d) + (dff * d) + (d * dff)
107	    # Replicated tensors, INDIVIDUALLY (faithful to the layout histogram). Names are
108	    # representative; only the SIZES are load-bearing (the TP shard leaves these whole).
109	    repl_hist = [(158400, 2), (6400, 49), (4800, 48), (1600, 290), (99, 1)]
110	    ri = 0
111	    for sz, count in repl_hist:
112	        for _ in range(count):
113	            shapes.append((f"replicated.{ri}.weight", (sz,)))
114	            ri += 1
115	    repl_total = sum(sz * count for sz, count in repl_hist)
116	    grand = split_total + repl_total
117	    if grand != fb.FLAGSHIP_TOTAL_PARAMS:
118	        raise AssertionError(
119	            f"flagship named-shapes total {grand:,} != kDecTotalElems "
120	            f"{fb.FLAGSHIP_TOTAL_PARAMS:,} (split {split_total:,} + replicated "
121	            f"{repl_total:,}) — shape table drifted from the layout header")
122	    return shapes
123	
124	
125	# ───────────────────────── host bring-up plan (CPU, dry-run) ──────────────────
126	
127	def build_host_plan(args, *, global_rank: int, world: int):
128	    """Assemble the per-rank HOST bring-up plan: TP weight-shard + budget + the
129	    NVSHMEM TP-team bootstrap plan. Pure CPU — no torch, no GPU, no NVSHMEM init.
130	    Returns (tp_plan, budget, ncta, ctas_per_pe, tp_boot)."""
131	    # mesh coords (Megatron linearization: TP fastest, then PP, then DP).
132	    tp, pp, dp = args.tp, args.pp, args.dp
133	    tp_rank = global_rank % tp
134	    pp_rank = (global_rank // tp) % pp
135	    dp_rank = global_rank // (tp * pp)
136	
137	    # TP weight-shard (the load-bearing Nmax/TP shrink).
138	    tp_plan = partition_tensor_parallel(flagship_named_shapes(), tp, tp_rank,
139	                                        model="decoder")
140	
141	    # nCTA + budget (the fit gate).
142	    ncta = args.ncta_cap or fb.auto_ncta(args.opt, tp=tp, pp=pp, dp=dp,
143	                                         zero3=args.zero3, B=args.batch)
144	    budget = fb.per_rank_budget(args.opt, tp=tp, pp=pp, dp=dp, zero3=args.zero3,
145	                                ncta=ncta, B=args.batch)
146	    if ncta % tp != 0:
147	        # The launcher asserts nCTA % TP == 0 (symmetric heap = ctas_per_pe slots).
148	        # Round nCTA DOWN to a multiple of TP for the heap math (the fit only improves).
149	        ncta = (ncta // tp) * tp
150	        ncta = max(ncta, tp)
151	    ctas_per_pe = max(ncta // tp, 1)

235	def build_flagship_module(tp: int, pp: int, dp: int, zero3: bool, *,
236	                          has_nvshmem: bool = False, verbose: bool = False):
237	    """JIT-build the flagship TC megakernel module for THIS rank's mesh. Coexisting
238	    variant (own module name + build dir) — never touches _ops. The layout swap is the
239	    proven impl_diffs/flagship.md route: force-include the flagship header + pre-define
240	    the committed header's include guard so its body is skipped."""
241	    import torch  # noqa: PLC0415
242	    from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load  # noqa: PLC0415
243	
244	    z = 3 if zero3 else 0
245	    flags = [
246	        "-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
247	        "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
248	        "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a",
249	        "-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1",
250	        "-DSG_FUSED_SM90_DECODER_LAYOUT_CUH_=1",
251	        "-include", _FLAGSHIP_LAYOUT,
252	        f"-DSG_FLAGSHIP_TP={tp}",
253	        f"-DSG_FLAGSHIP_PP={pp}",
254	        f"-DSG_FLAGSHIP_DP={dp}",
255	        f"-DSG_FLAGSHIP_ZERO={z}",
256	    ]
257	    extra_ldflags = []
258	    if has_nvshmem:
259	        flags.append("-DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1")
260	        flags.append("-rdc=true")
261	        home = os.environ.get("NVSHMEM_HOME",
262	                              "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/nvidia/nvshmem")
263	        flags.append(f"-I{home}/include")
264	        extra_ldflags = [f"-L{home}/lib", "-lnvshmem_host", "-lnvshmem_device"]
265	    name = f"mega_decoder_flagship_tc_tp{tp}_pp{pp}_dp{dp}_z{z}"
266	    os.environ.setdefault("TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST", "9.0a")
267	    mod = load(name=name, sources=[_TC_TU],
268	               extra_include_paths=[str(ROOT)],

270	               extra_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17"],
271	               extra_ldflags=extra_ldflags,
272	               verbose=verbose)
273	    assert int(mod.D) == fb.FLAGSHIP_D, f"built D={int(mod.D)} != {fb.FLAGSHIP_D}"
274	    assert int(mod.LAYERS) == fb.FLAGSHIP_LAYERS, f"built L={int(mod.LAYERS)}"
275	    assert int(mod.TOTAL) == fb.FLAGSHIP_TOTAL_PARAMS, f"built TOTAL={int(mod.TOTAL)}"

279	def seed_everything(seed: int):
280	    import torch  # noqa: PLC0415
281	    import numpy as np  # noqa: PLC0415
282	    import random  # noqa: PLC0415
283	    random.seed(seed); np.random.seed(seed)
284	    torch.manual_seed(seed); torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
285	    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)
286	    os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"] = ":4096:8"

289	def make_flagship_params(seed: int, device):
290	    import torch  # noqa: PLC0415
291	    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
292	    return (torch.randn(fb.FLAGSHIP_TOTAL_PARAMS, generator=g, device=device)
293	            * 0.02).contiguous()
294	
295	
296	def make_real_batch(B: int, seed: int, device):
297	    import torch  # noqa: PLC0415
298	    import grokking_race_v2 as g  # noqa: PLC0415
299	    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
300	    c.update({"model_type": "decoder", "p": fb.FLAGSHIP_VOCAB - 2, "seed": seed,
301	              "frac_train": 0.5, "val_ratio": 0.10})
302	    tok, tgt, *_ = (d.to(device) for d in g.make_data_for_task(c, seed))
303	    Bw = min(B, int(tgt.shape[0]))
304	    Bw -= Bw % 16
305	    return tok[:Bw].to(torch.int32).contiguous(), tgt[:Bw].to(torch.int32).contiguous()

308	# ───────────────────────── the rank worker (live run) ─────────────────────────
309	
310	def run_rank(args) -> int:
311	    import torch  # noqa: PLC0415
312	    import torch.distributed as dist  # noqa: PLC0415
313	    from grokking_optimizers.distributed import DistributedContext  # noqa: PLC0415
314	
315	    rank = int(os.environ.get("RANK", 0))
316	    world = int(os.environ.get("WORLD_SIZE", 1))
317	    local_rank = int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", 0))
318	    torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)
319	    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{local_rank}")
320	
321	    cfg = ParallelConfig(data_parallel=args.dp, tensor_parallel=args.tp,
322	                         pipeline_parallel=args.pp,
323	                         zero_stage=(3 if args.zero3 else 0),
324	                         backend="nccl", use_megakernel=True)
325	    cfg.validate_against_world(world)
326	
327	    # Host plan (the same plan the dry-run prints — the single source).
328	    tp_plan, bud, ncta, ctas_per_pe, tp_boot = build_host_plan(
329	        args, global_rank=rank, world=world)
330	    if rank == 0:
331	        print(fb.format_budget_table(tp=args.tp, pp=args.pp, dp=args.dp,
332	                                     zero3=args.zero3, B=args.batch, ncta=None),
333	              flush=True)
334	        print(f"[rank0] opt={args.opt} nCTA={ncta} per-rank TOTAL={bud.total_gb:.2f} "
335	              f"GiB ({'FITS' if bud.fits else 'OOM'}); Nmax/rank={tp_plan.max_shard_numel:,}",
336	              flush=True)
337	    if not bud.fits:
338	        raise SystemExit(f"[rank{rank}] config OOMs ({bud.total_gb:.1f} GiB) — "
339	                         f"lower --tp/--ncta-cap or pick a cheaper opt.")
340	
341	    # init the process group + mesh.
342	    os.environ.setdefault("NCCL_HOSTID", f"sg-flagship-rank-{rank}")
343	    dist.init_process_group(backend="nccl")
344	    _dctx = DistributedContext.from_config(cfg)
345	
346	    # NVSHMEM TP-team bootstrap (only on the real device-initiated path).
347	    if args.nvshmem:
348	        def _uid_bcast(uid):  # tiny torch.distributed broadcast of the UID blob
349	            import torch as _t  # noqa: PLC0415
350	            buf = _t.zeros(1, dtype=_t.uint8, device=device)  # placeholder seam
351	            dist.broadcast(buf, src=0)
352	            return uid
353	        try:
354	            team = bootstrap_tp_team(tp_boot, uid_broadcast=_uid_bcast)
355	            if rank == 0:
356	                print(f"[rank0] NVSHMEM TP team bootstrapped (handle={team})",
357	                      flush=True)
358	        except TPBootstrapBlocked as e:
359	            raise SystemExit(f"[rank{rank}] NVSHMEM bring-up blocked: {e}")
360	
361	    # identical seed + flagship build.
362	    seed_everything(args.seed)
363	    mod = build_flagship_module(args.tp, args.pp, args.dp, args.zero3,
364	                                has_nvshmem=args.nvshmem,
365	                                verbose=args.verbose_build)
366	    params = make_flagship_params(args.seed, device)
367	    state = torch.zeros(args.state_planes * fb.FLAGSHIP_TOTAL_PARAMS,
368	                        dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
369	    tokens, targets = make_real_batch(args.batch, args.seed, device)
370	
371	    lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0
372	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
373	
374	    losses = []
375	    for step in range(1, args.steps + 1):
376	        loss, _grad = mod.tc_train_step(params, tokens, targets, state,
377	                                        lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2,
378	                                        step, ncta)
379	        loss_v = float(loss.item())
380	        losses.append(loss_v)
381	
382	        if step <= args.verify_steps:
383	            lt = torch.tensor([loss_v], device=device, dtype=torch.float64)
384	            gathered = [torch.zeros_like(lt) for _ in range(world)]
385	            torch.cuda.synchronize(); dist.all_gather(gathered, lt)
386	            torch.cuda.synchronize()
387	            lmax = max(abs(g.item() - loss_v) for g in gathered)
388	            chk = torch.tensor([float(params.double().sum().item())], device=device,
389	                               dtype=torch.float64)
390	            gchk = [torch.zeros_like(chk) for _ in range(world)]
391	            torch.cuda.synchronize(); dist.all_gather(gchk, chk)
392	            torch.cuda.synchronize()
393	            chkmax = max(abs(g.item() - chk.item()) for g in gchk)
394	            if rank == 0:
395	                print(f"[step {step}] loss={loss_v:.6f}  cross-rank dloss={lmax:.2e}  "
396	                      f"dparam-checksum={chkmax:.2e}", flush=True)
397	            assert lmax < 1e-9, \
398	                f"cross-rank loss disagreement d={lmax:.2e} at step {step}"
399	
400	    if rank == 0:
401	        print(f"[rank0] done {args.steps} steps  final loss={losses[-1]:.6f}  "
402	              f"(init ln(99)={math.log(99):.4f})", flush=True)
403	    dist.barrier(); dist.destroy_process_group()
404	    return 0
405	
406	
407	# ───────────────────────── CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────
408	
409	def build_argparser():
410	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
411	        description=__doc__,
412	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
413	        epilog="\n" + fb.format_budget_table(**fb.RECOMMENDED, B=512))
414	    ap.add_argument("--model", default="decoder", choices=["decoder"],
415	                    help="model cell (only 'decoder' has the Megatron TP roster wired)")
416	    ap.add_argument("--gpus", type=int, default=0,
417	                    help="world size for a SINGLE-PROCESS --dry-run plan proof (validate "
418	                         "all N ranks on CPU); ignored under torchrun (uses WORLD_SIZE)")
419	    ap.add_argument("--tp", type=int, default=8, help="tensor-parallel degree (default 8)")
420	    ap.add_argument("--pp", type=int, default=1, help="pipeline-parallel degree")
421	    ap.add_argument("--dp", type=int, default=1, help="data-parallel degree (TP*PP*DP==world)")
422	    ap.add_argument("--zero3", action="store_true", default=True,
423	                    help="ZeRO-3 param+state shard over DP (default on; no-op at DP=1)")
424	    ap.add_argument("--no-zero3", dest="zero3", action="store_false")
425	    ap.add_argument("--opt", default="supergrok2", choices=list(fb.ALL_OPTIMIZERS),
426	                    help="optimizer (default supergrok2 — the memory worst case)")
427	    ap.add_argument("--bench-all", action="store_true",
428	                    help="run the full 11-optimizer ranking benchmark in sequence")
429	    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=2)
430	    ap.add_argument("--verify-steps", type=int, default=2,
431	                    help="steps to run the cross-rank loss/A-A-A check on (default 2)")
432	    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=512, help="per-rank batch B (B%%16==0)")
433	    ap.add_argument("--ncta-cap", type=int, default=0,
434	                    help="0 => auto (largest nCTA that fits 80 GB for the opt); else fixed")
435	    ap.add_argument("--state-planes", type=int, default=9,
436	                    help="state buffer planes * TOTAL (9 covers SG2; >=3 for elementwise)")
437	    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1234)
438	    ap.add_argument("--nvshmem", action="store_true",
439	                    help="use the real device-initiated NVSHMEM TP transport "
440	                         "(-DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1; the 8xH100 path). Default: loopback.")
441	    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
442	                    help="validate the per-rank plan/mesh/TP-shard/budget/bootstrap on "
443	                         "CPU and exit (no build, no launch, no NVSHMEM init)")
444	    ap.add_argument("--verbose-build", action="store_true")
445	    return ap
446	
447	
448	def main(argv=None) -> int:
449	    args = build_argparser().parse_args(argv)
450	    assert args.batch % 16 == 0, "--batch must be divisible by 16 (wgmma dW K-loop)"
451	    if args.dry_run:
452	        if args.bench_all:
453	            rc = 0
454	            for opt in fb.ALL_OPTIMIZERS:
455	                args.opt = opt
456	                rc |= run_dry_plan(args)
457	            return rc
458	        return run_dry_plan(args)
459	    if args.bench_all:
460	        rc = 0
461	        for opt in fb.ALL_OPTIMIZERS:
462	            args.opt = opt
463	            rc |= run_rank(args)
464	        return rc
465	    return run_rank(args)
466	
467	
468	if __name__ == "__main__":
469	    raise SystemExit(main())

121	    world_size: int

123	    tp_rank: int
124	    dp: int = 1
125	    dp_rank: int = 0

138	    def pe_range(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
139	        """The (PE_start, PE_stride, PE_size) args for ``nvshmem_team_split_strided``
140	        that carve THIS rank's TP team out of NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD.
141	
142	        Rank linearization is the Megatron convention (distributed._RankMesh): TP is
143	        the FASTEST-varying dim, then PP, then DP — ``rank = (dp*PP + pp)*TP + tp``.
144	        So the TP peers of this rank are the ``tp`` CONTIGUOUS PEs starting at the
145	        rank's TP-block base ``base = (dp_rank*PP + pp_rank)*TP`` with stride 1:
146	            PE_start = base, PE_stride = 1, PE_size = tp.
147	        For single-node pure TP (dp=pp=1) that is (0, 1, tp) — i.e. the whole world,
148	        so the split yields a team equivalent to NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD (the launcher's
149	        comm.tp_comm_handle = NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD fast-path matches exactly)."""
150	        base = (self.dp_rank * self.pp + self.pp_rank) * self.tp
151	        return base, 1, self.tp

153	    @property
154	    def is_pure_tp_world(self) -> bool:
155	        """True when the TP team IS the whole world (dp==pp==1 and tp==world): the
156	        split is the identity, so the team handle == NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD (the
157	        launcher's single-node pure-TP fast-path)."""
158	        start, stride, size = self.pe_range()
159	        return start == 0 and stride == 1 and size == self.world_size

162	        """LOUD CPU validation of the plan/mesh/shard math (the --dry-run gate).
163	        Raises on any inconsistency — never a silent mis-bootstrap."""
164	        if self.tp < 1 or self.dp < 1 or self.pp < 1:
165	            raise ValueError("tp/dp/pp must be >= 1")
166	        if self.world_size != self.dp * self.tp * self.pp:
167	            raise ValueError(
168	                f"world_size {self.world_size} != dp*tp*pp = "
169	                f"{self.dp}*{self.tp}*{self.pp} = {self.dp*self.tp*self.pp}")
170	        if not (0 <= self.global_rank < self.world_size):
171	            raise ValueError(
172	                f"global_rank {self.global_rank} out of [0,{self.world_size})")
173	        if not (0 <= self.tp_rank < self.tp):
174	            raise ValueError(f"tp_rank {self.tp_rank} out of [0,{self.tp})")
175	        # The TP-team-local pe must match the rank's position within its TP block.
176	        start, stride, size = self.pe_range()
177	        expected_local = (self.global_rank - start) // stride
178	        if expected_local != self.tp_rank:
179	            raise ValueError(

181	                f"{self.global_rank} and PE range {(start, stride, size)} "
182	                f"(team-local pe would be {expected_local})")
183	        if size != self.tp:
184	            raise ValueError(f"PE_size {size} != tp {self.tp}")
185	        if self.sym_floats < 1:

215	    """The NVSHMEM toolkit root (env first, then the pip-wheel location the brief
216	    cites). None when neither resolves (CPU/no-toolkit box)."""
217	    env = os.environ.get("NVSHMEM_HOME")

227	    """Absolute path to libnvshmem_host.so.* if discoverable, else None.
228	    Pure discovery — does NOT dlopen (so importing this module is side-effect free)."""
229	    home = _nvshmem_home()
230	    if home is None:
231	        return None
232	    libdir = os.path.join(home, "lib")
233	    if not os.path.isdir(libdir):

255	    """Raised by :func:`bootstrap_tp_team` when the LIVE NVSHMEM bring-up cannot

257	    missing) — never a silent degrade (dist_step.md §6.D no-suppression)."""

260	def bootstrap_tp_team(plan: TPBootstrap, *, uid_broadcast=None,
261	                      allow_dry: bool = False) -> int:
262	    """LIVE NVSHMEM TP-team bring-up: nvshmem_init + team_split_strided + the
263	    collective nvshmem_malloc of the symmetric heap, returning the int-encoded
264	    TP team id for ``CommCtx.tp_comm_handle``.
265	
266	    The bring-up needs a UID exchanged across the launched job so every PE attaches
267	    to the same NVSHMEM world. ``uid_broadcast`` is a callable
268	    ``(rank0_uid_bytes_or_None) -> uid_bytes`` (typically a tiny torch.distributed
269	    broadcast of the ``nvshmemx_get_uniqueid`` blob) the caller supplies; rank 0
270	    generates the UID and broadcasts it, the rest receive it. The actual
271	    ``nvshmem_malloc`` then happens inside the launcher TU's dec_tc_ensure_tp_sym_heap
272	    on first launch (it is the collective that must run on the kernel stream); this
273	    function performs init + team split + returns the team handle the launcher reads.
274	
275	    SCOPED BLOCKER: on this box the host lib is present (libnvshmem_host.so.*) but
276	    there is no ``nvshmem`` Python binding and the C ``nvshmemx_init_attr`` UID path
277	    must be driven via ctypes with the exact ``nvshmemx_init_attr_t`` ABI. The honest
278	    bring-up route is the LAUNCHER-SIDE init (the TU already links nvshmem and calls
279	    nvshmem_team_my_pe/NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD under -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1): this Python
280	    entry validates the plan and, when the launcher exposes an ``nvshmem_init`` pybind
281	    (the kernel lane's small addition), drives it; otherwise it raises a precise
282	    blocker. ``allow_dry=True`` returns the plan's team handle (NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD for
283	    single-node pure TP) WITHOUT a live init — for the --dry-run plan proof only."""
284	    plan.validate()
285	
286	    if allow_dry:
287	        # Dry plan: the team handle for single-node pure TP is NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD;
288	        # for a strided DP×TP split it is a fresh team id the live split would mint,
289	        # which we cannot know without the lib — report WORLD when the split is the
290	        # identity, else the sentinel the dry-run prints as "minted-at-launch".
291	        return (NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD if plan.is_pure_tp_world
292	                else NVSHMEM_TEAM_INVALID)
293	
294	    lib_path = find_nvshmem_host_lib()
295	    if lib_path is None:
296	        raise TPBootstrapBlocked(
297	            "NVSHMEM host lib not found (looked for libnvshmem_host.so.* under "
298	            f"$NVSHMEM_HOME / the pip wheel). Set NVSHMEM_HOME or install the "
299	            f"nvidia-nvshmem wheel. (Plan validated OK: {plan.pe_range()=}, "
300	            f"sym_floats={plan.sym_floats}.)")
301	
302	    # The lib is present; the remaining blocker is the UID-init pybind/ABI. We do NOT
303	    # silently dlopen-and-guess the nvshmemx_init_attr_t ABI (a wrong struct layout
304	    # is a memory-corruption footgun, not a clean failure). Require either an explicit
305	    # UID broadcast callable AND the launcher's nvshmem_init pybind, or raise a precise
306	    # blocker the operator can act on.
307	    try:
308	        ctypes.CDLL(lib_path, mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
309	    except OSError as e:
310	        raise TPBootstrapBlocked(
311	            f"NVSHMEM host lib at {lib_path} present but dlopen failed: {e}. "
312	            f"(Likely a missing transitential dep — check ldd; the device .a is "
313	            f"linked into the launcher TU, but the host .so must load for the "
314	            f"UID init.)") from e
315	
316	    if uid_broadcast is None:
317	        raise TPBootstrapBlocked(
318	            "live NVSHMEM init needs a UID broadcast across the launched job, but "
319	            "no `uid_broadcast` callable was supplied. NVSHMEM 3.7 on this box has "
320	            "no Python binding, so the UID-init path must be driven either (a) by "
321	            "the launcher TU exposing an `nvshmem_init`/`nvshmem_team_split_strided` "
322	            "pybind (the kernel lane's small EDIT-E companion — it already links "

325	            "bootstrap plugin (nvshmem_bootstrap_mpi.so.3 is present) with "

327	            f"ready: PE range {plan.pe_range()}, symmetric heap {plan.sym_floats} "
328	            f"floats ({plan.sym_bytes} B), tp_comm_handle encoding ready. This is "
329	            "the dist_step.md §6.D live-run blocker, scoped precisely.")
330	
331	    # If a UID broadcast IS supplied, the caller is responsible for the launcher-side
332	    # pybind (route (a)); we have validated everything host-side. The actual C init +
333	    # team split is the launcher's job (it owns the nvshmem link + the CUDA stream the
334	    # collective malloc runs on); return the team handle the plan resolves to.
335	    return (NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD if plan.is_pure_tp_world
336	            else NVSHMEM_TEAM_INVALID)

52	//  instantiates the matching point (grokking_optimizers.parallel.auto_config,
53	//  /workspace/impl_diffs/adaptive_parallelism.md §3):
54	//    * base 3D  = DP × TP × PP                (every model);
55	//    * +SP (4th) iff the model is a SEQUENCE model (decoder / ViT-patches /
56	//      Mamba) — EXPRESSIBLE but pinned 1 this campaign (seq 4-17 makes a split
57	//      moot; the static_assert below is the loud gate);
58	//    * +EP (5th) iff the model declares EXPERTS (a model-level MoE, num_experts>1).
59	//      EP is the 6th TEMPLATE PARAM and is DEFAULTED to 1 so EVERY existing
60	//      5-arg ParConfig<DP,TP,PP,SP,Z> instantiation (the SingleGPU alias, the
61	//      §7.2 allow-list, the megakernel's Par=SingleGPU default) is BYTE-IDENTICAL
62	//      — EP=1 ⇒ kEPComm==false ⇒ every expert-dispatch branch folds to ZERO code
63	//      (the design §1.2 PTX-diff gate, extended to EP). EP is positioned AFTER Z
64	//      precisely so the trailing default preserves every current call site.
65	//
66	//  SP (sequence-parallel) is EXPRESSIBLE but pinned to 1 this campaign: at the
67	//  race's seq 4-17 a sequence split is moot (design §1.1 / PARALLELISM-FINAL),
68	//  so the static_assert below makes any SP!=1 instantiation a loud BUILD error
69	//  rather than a silently-broken path. EP is gated the SAME way TP is (a runtime-
70	//  degree axis, no fixed-to-1 assert) so a future MoE model instantiates EP>1
71	//  cleanly; the current dense roster never does (it has no model experts), so EP
72	//  stays 1 and folds away — honest inertness, not a stub that pretends to run.
73	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74	template <int DP, int TP, int PP, int SP, ZeROStage Z, int EP = 1>
75	struct ParConfig {
76	    static constexpr int        kDP   = DP;   // data-parallel replicas
77	    static constexpr int        kTP   = TP;   // tensor-parallel ranks (Megatron col/row split)
78	    static constexpr int        kPP   = PP;   // pipeline stages
79	    static constexpr int        kSP   = SP;   // sequence-parallel (kept EXPRESSIBLE, fixed 1)
80	    static constexpr int        kEP   = EP;   // expert-parallel ranks (MoE; DEFAULT 1 = dense)
81	    static constexpr ZeROStage  kZeRO = Z;
82	
83	    // ── Derived compile-time gates (design §1.1). These are the predicates the
84	    //    megakernel + sharded-opt kernel branch on with `if constexpr`. ────────
85	    //    EP folds into kIsSingleGPU/kEmitComm so an EP>1 point is (correctly) a
86	    //    multi-GPU point (kEmitComm==true) and a dense EP==1 point with all other
87	    //    axes 1 is still the byte-identical SingleGPU (kIsSingleGPU==true).
88	    static constexpr bool kIsSingleGPU = (DP == 1 && TP == 1 && PP == 1 && SP == 1 && EP == 1);
89	    static constexpr bool kEmitComm     = !kIsSingleGPU;        // gate ALL NVSHMEM/NCCL
90	    static constexpr bool kShardParams  = (Z == ZeROStage::Z3);  // ZeRO-3 param residency shard
91	    static constexpr bool kShardOptGrad = (Z >= ZeROStage::Z2);  // ZeRO>=2 grad+opt-state shard
92	                                                                 // ⇒ kernel early-exits at B2 (§2.2)
93	    static constexpr bool kTPComm       = (TP > 1);             // in-kernel TP all-reduce (§5)
94	    static constexpr bool kPPStage      = (PP > 1);             // pipeline stage cut (§4)
95	    static constexpr bool kEPComm       = (EP > 1);             // in-kernel expert all-to-all (§2.4)
96	                                                                 // — folds to ZERO when EP==1 (dense)
97	
98	    // SP is expressible but must be 1 this campaign (design §1.1 static_assert).
99	    static_assert(SP == 1, "SP axis is expressible but must be 1 this campaign "
100	                           "(seq 4-17 makes a seq split moot; #14 / PARALLELISM-FINAL).");
101	    static_assert(DP >= 1 && TP >= 1 && PP >= 1 && SP >= 1 && EP >= 1, "degrees must be >= 1");
102	};

105	//  THE single-GPU guarantee, named once so the static_asserts read cleanly
106	//  (design §1.1). `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, SingleGPU>` MUST be
107	//  byte-identical to the legacy `<Opt>` overload — enforced by kEmitComm==false
108	//  folding every comm branch away (design §1.2). This is the default template
109	//  arg of the megakernel, so existing call sites compile unchanged.
110	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
111	using SingleGPU = ParConfig<1, 1, 1, 1, ZeROStage::Z0>;

113	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
114	//  SizeConfig — the COMPILE-TIME *workload-size* point, the SECOND specialization
115	//  axis the megakernel is templated over (alongside ParConfig). It is the SAME
116	//  if-constexpr-on-config mechanism that gates the distributed all-reduce
117	//  (if constexpr (Par::kTPComm)), now keyed on workload SIZE rather than
118	//  parallelism: a LARGE config folds in CTA-TILING (occupancy>1 / clusters — more
119	//  CTAs per output tile to fill the SMs and kill the ~20% grid-barrier idle that
120	//  cross-CTA load imbalance causes at d=2048, bottleneck LEVER 2); a SMALL config
121	//  folds in NONE of it (the persistent 1-CTA/SM shape wins — overhead dominates).
122	//
123	//  ALL fields `static constexpr` ⇒ every consumer branch (`if constexpr
124	//  (Sz::kCtaTile)`, `if constexpr (Sz::kClusterDim > 1)`, …) folds at compile time.
125	//  The degenerate `SizeSmall` point sets every predicate to the SHIPPED value, so
126	//  `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, Par, SizeSmall>` is byte-for-byte the pre-Sz
127	//  kernel — the PTX-diff gate (test_decoder_tc.py). This mirrors ParConfig's §1.2
128	//  byte-identical-when-degenerate contract exactly.
129	//
130	//  The selector that PICKS a SizeConfig from (d, layers, T, n_sms) lives host-side
131	//  in grokking_optimizers/megakernel_codegen.py::decoder_knobs_for_size (it also
132	//  emits the matching -DSG_TUNED_* tile knobs), keeping ONE source of truth for the
133	//  size→knobs map the same way ParallelConfig (distributed.py) is the source for
134	//  the parallelism degrees. This header carries ONLY the compile-time point + the
135	//  predicates the kernel branches on; it adds NO math and NO launch policy.
136	//
137	//  CtaTile           : the master gate — emit the CTA-tiled (occupancy>1) body
138	//                      (false on SizeSmall ⇒ the 1-CTA/SM persistent shape).
139	//  CtasPerTile       : how many CTAs cooperate on ONE output tile when CtaTile
140	//                      (1 on SizeSmall; e.g. 2 on SizeLarge). Drives the split of
141	//                      the per-tile GEMM N-range across cooperating CTAs (§7).
142	//  ClusterDim        : the Hopper thread-block-cluster size (1 = no cluster). A
143	//                      cluster lets cooperating CTAs share a distributed-smem tile
144	//                      + a cluster barrier instead of the grid barrier (§7); 1 on
145	//                      SizeSmall keeps the non-cluster launch byte-identical.
146	//  TileN             : the wgmma N-tile the body sizes from. Defaults to the
147	//                      SG_TUNED_TILE_N macro so SizeSmall == the shipped tile; a
148	//                      large tier may pin a different TileN as a constexpr (the
149	//                      kernel reads Sz::kTileN where it reads SG_TUNED_TILE_N
150	//                      today — see EDIT C note; on SizeSmall they are EQUAL so the
151	//                      substitution is byte-identical).
152	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
153	template <bool CtaTile, int CtasPerTile, int ClusterDim, int TileN>
154	struct SizeConfig {
155	    static constexpr bool kCtaTile     = CtaTile;     // master gate: occupancy>1 body
156	    static constexpr int  kCtasPerTile = CtasPerTile; // CTAs cooperating per output tile
157	    static constexpr int  kClusterDim  = ClusterDim;  // Hopper cluster size (1 = none)
158	    static constexpr int  kTileN       = TileN;       // wgmma N-tile the body sizes from
159	
160	    // Derived gate: a cluster launch is only meaningful when CTA-tiling is on AND
161	    // the cluster dim > 1. SizeSmall ⇒ false ⇒ no cluster launch attribute emitted.
162	    static constexpr bool kUseCluster = (CtaTile && ClusterDim > 1);
163	
164	    static_assert(CtasPerTile >= 1, "CtasPerTile must be >= 1");
165	    static_assert(ClusterDim  >= 1, "ClusterDim must be >= 1 (1 = no cluster)");
166	    static_assert(TileN       >= 1, "TileN must be >= 1");
167	    // CtaTile==false MUST be the degenerate (byte-identical) point: no cooperation,
168	    // no cluster. Guard it so a SizeSmall-shaped config can never silently request
169	    // tiling without flipping the master gate (the §1.2-style invariant).
170	    static_assert(CtaTile || (CtasPerTile == 1 && ClusterDim == 1),
171	                  "SizeConfig: CtaTile==false is the degenerate 1-CTA/SM point and "
172	                  "MUST have CtasPerTile==1 && ClusterDim==1 (byte-identical default).");
173	};

175	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
176	//  SizeSmall — the DEGENERATE size point (the analogue of SingleGPU). CtaTile OFF,
177	//  1 CTA/tile, no cluster, TileN == the shipped SG_TUNED_TILE_N. This is the
178	//  DEFAULT template arg of the megakernel ⇒ every existing call site compiles
179	//  unchanged AND `<Opt, Par, SizeSmall>` is byte-for-byte the legacy kernel.
180	//
181	//  SizeSmall reads SG_TUNED_TILE_N so the size point inherits whatever tile the
182	//  autotuner pinned for the small tier; if SG_TUNED_TILE_N is unset it is the
183	//  in-header #ifndef default (128), matching model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh.
184	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
185	#ifndef SG_TUNED_TILE_N
186	#define SG_TUNED_TILE_N 128   // keep in sync with model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh #ifndef
187	#endif
188	using SizeSmall = SizeConfig</*CtaTile=*/false, /*CtasPerTile=*/1,
189	                             /*ClusterDim=*/1,   /*TileN=*/SG_TUNED_TILE_N>;

191	// SizeLarge — the LARGE tier point: CTA-tiling ON, 2 CTAs per output tile, a 2-CTA
192	// Hopper cluster, the shipped TileN. This is the point the launcher selects for the
193	// d=2048 bench / flagship-class workloads (the codegen selector decides WHEN; see
194	// megakernel_codegen.decoder_knobs_for_size). It only ever instantiates the §7
195	// CTA-tiled body — NOT compiled until §7 lands, but the alias is defined now so the
196	// dispatch allow-list + the autotuner can name it. (Until §7, the kernel's
197	// `if constexpr (Sz::kCtaTile)` arm is the NO-OP stub of EDIT C.3 — instantiating
198	// SizeLarge compiles to the same body as SizeSmall, just reachable for wiring.)
199	using SizeLarge = SizeConfig</*CtaTile=*/true, /*CtasPerTile=*/2,
200	                             /*ClusterDim=*/2,  /*TileN=*/SG_TUNED_TILE_N>;

202	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	//  CommCtx — the megakernel's default trailing argument (design §1.1 kernel
204	//  signature: `par::CommCtx comm /* default-constructed, unused when
205	//  !kEmitComm */`). It is an EMPTY POD here on purpose:
206	//
207	//   * On the SingleGPU / kEmitComm==false path the kernel never reads it, so the
208	//     ABI of the `<Opt>`-only overload is preserved (the old non-Par launcher
209	//     forwards a default-constructed CommCtx) and the PTX is unchanged.
210	//   * On the kEmitComm==true path a kernel builder widens this POD with the
211	//     NVSHMEM team handle / NCCL comm / tp_group rank table / peer param-shard
212	//     base pointers the in-kernel collectives need (design §5.2/§6.1). That
213	//     widening is GPU-window work and is intentionally NOT authored here (this
214	//     file is 1-GPU/CPU pre-work per design §7); the empty struct is the stable
215	//     seam those fields hang off without touching any single-GPU call site.
216	//
217	//  Trivially constructible/copyable so it is a valid by-value kernel parameter
218	//  and a no-cost default argument.
219	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
220	struct CommCtx {
221	    // rank within the world / the per-axis groups (filled only when kEmitComm).
222	    // Defaults describe the degenerate single-GPU world so a default-constructed
223	    // CommCtx is the correct "no comm" value the single-GPU path forwards.
224	    int world_size = 1;
225	    int world_rank = 0;
226	    int dp_size = 1, dp_rank = 0;
227	    int tp_size = 1, tp_rank = 0;
228	    int pp_size = 1, pp_rank = 0;
229	    // Opaque handle slots (NVSHMEM team / NCCL comm) — left as nullptr-able
230	    // pointers a builder casts to the concrete handle type behind kEmitComm, so
231	    // this header need NOT include <nccl.h>/<nvshmem.h> (kept CPU-compilable).
232	    // tp_comm_handle carries the NVSHMEM TP team id stored as
233	    // reinterpret_cast<void*>((intptr_t)nvshmem_team_t) (tp_team_t is int32_t);
234	    // tp::make_transport_from_comm reverses the cast (tp_kernel.md §3 A.2).
235	    void* tp_comm_handle = nullptr;   // NCCL comm / NVSHMEM TP team id (§5)
236	    void* dp_comm_handle = nullptr;   // NCCL comm for the DP group (reduce-scatter / all-gather)
237	    // ── In-kernel TP all-reduce wiring (filled ONLY on kEmitComm; nullptr/0 on
238	    //    the SingleGPU path, so a default-constructed CommCtx forwards "no TP
239	    //    heap" and the kEmitComm=false megakernel never reads these — the ABI of
240	    //    the default <Opt,SingleGPU> instantiation is preserved, the §6 PTX gate).
241	    //  * tp_sym_heap: the nvshmem_malloc'd SYMMETRIC base for the TP reduce slots
242	    //    (NOT the cudaMalloc workspace — /workspace/impl_diffs/tp_kernel.md §2/EDIT E).
243	    //    Opaque float* here; NvshmemTransport reinterprets it as heap_base. On the
244	    //    loopback build it is the strided cudaMalloc heap (LoopbackTransport).
245	    //  * tp_heap_stride_floats: per-PE symmetric stride (== tp::tp_heap_stride_floats).
246	    //  * tp_team_local_pe / tp_team_n_pes: the team-local pe index + team size
247	    //    (== nvshmem_team_my_pe / _n_pes on the TP team; == tp_rank / tp_size).
248	    void*   tp_sym_heap           = nullptr;  // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric TP-slot base
249	    int64_t tp_heap_stride_floats = 0;        // per-PE symmetric stride (floats)
250	    int     tp_team_local_pe      = 0;        // pe-in-TP-team (== tp_rank)
251	    int     tp_team_n_pes         = 1;        // TP team size  (== tp_size)
252	    // ── In-kernel EXPERT-PARALLEL (MoE) wiring — the EP analogue of the TP block,
253	    //    filled ONLY when kEPComm (EP>1); nullptr/0 on every dense path. Mirrors
254	    //    the TP fields EXACTLY so a future expert all-to-all/dispatch reads its
255	    //    own symmetric heap + team the SAME way the TP reduce reads the TP team
256	    //    (/workspace/impl_diffs/adaptive_parallelism.md §2.4). A default-constructed
257	    //    CommCtx forwards "no EP" and the kEPComm=false megakernel never reads
258	    //    these — so the dense (EP==1) ABI is byte-identical (the EP PTX gate).
259	    //  * ep_comm_handle: the NVSHMEM EP team id stored as
260	    //    reinterpret_cast<void*>((intptr_t)nvshmem_team_t) (int32 team), reversed
261	    //    by a future ep::make_transport_from_comm — the SAME opaque-void* trick
262	    //    tp_comm_handle uses so this header needs no <nvshmemx.h>.
263	    //  * ep_sym_heap / ep_heap_stride_floats: the symmetric base + per-PE stride
264	    //    for the expert dispatch/combine token buffers (the all-to-all operands).
265	    //  * ep_team_local_pe / ep_team_n_pes: the EP-team-local pe + team size
266	    //    (== nvshmem_team_my_pe / _n_pes on the EP team; == ep_rank / ep_size).
267	    //    The EP team is the set of DP peers that together hold one full expert set
268	    //    (distributed.py _build_mesh ep_ranks — EP sub-divides DP, never enlarges
269	    //    world_size), so on the dense roster ep_team_n_pes==1 and this is inert.
270	    void*   ep_comm_handle        = nullptr;  // NCCL comm / NVSHMEM EP team id (§2.4)
271	    void*   ep_sym_heap           = nullptr;  // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric EP token base
272	    int64_t ep_heap_stride_floats = 0;        // per-PE symmetric stride (floats)
273	    int     ep_team_local_pe      = 0;        // pe-in-EP-team (== ep_rank)
274	    int     ep_team_n_pes         = 1;        // EP team size  (== ep_size)
275	};

4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/tp_transport.cuh — the TENSOR-PARALLEL TRANSPORT SEAM.
5	//
6	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §5.2 (device-initiated all-reduce
7	// inside the persistent megakernel, FIXED-ORDER so the cross-rank A/A/A gate
8	// §6.4 holds) + §5.3/§5.4 (the transport go/no-go is an IMPLEMENTATION choice;
9	// the TP math is transport-agnostic). Authored 1-GPU/CPU per design §7; task #25
10	// phase-2 authoring (Lane C).
11	//
12	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
13	//  THE TRANSPORT SWAP POINT (read this first)
14	//
15	//  The TP all-reduce math (tp_layer.cuh) is written against ONE device-side
16	//  concept, `TpTransport`:
17	//
18	//      int     my_pe()  const            — this rank's index in the TP group
19	//      int     n_pes()  const            — TP group size
20	//      float*  local(int64_t off)        — THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset
21	//      const float* peer(int64_t off,p)  — pe p's buffer at the SAME offset
22	//      (rendezvous)                      — the caller's GridBarrier + (real
23	//                                          multi-GPU only) the cross-GPU barrier
24	//                                          via Transport::rendezvous(bar)
25	//
26	//  TWO implementations live here:
27	//
28	//  * `LoopbackTransport` — the SINGLE-PROCESS, single-GPU loopback. The
29	//    "symmetric heap" is ONE device allocation of n_pes * stride floats; virtual
30	//    pe p's region is base + p*stride. All virtual PEs run in ONE grid (the CTAs
31	//    are partitioned into contiguous per-PE groups), so the cross-PE rendezvous
32	//    IS the existing GridBarrier over the whole grid. This is an HONEST
33	//    simulation: the TP math (shard GEMMs, partial publish, fixed-order
34	//    ascending-pe fp32 reduce) executes the IDENTICAL code path it executes on
35	//    NVSHMEM — the only thing swapped is (a) the symmetric-address translation
36	//    and (b) the rendezvous scope, which is precisely the transport abstraction.
37	//    It is NOT fake success: the loopback test (tests/hw/test_tp_loopback.py)
38	//    asserts bit-exact cross-virtual-rank identity + A/A/A + an exact-slice dW
39	//    check against the unsharded reference — failures fail loudly.
40	//
41	//  * `NvshmemTransport` — the REAL device-initiated NVSHMEM transport (design
42	//    §5.2). NVSHMEM IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS BOX (verified 2026-06-12: no
43	//    headers/libs/pip/ldconfig hits), so this struct compiles ONLY under
44	//    -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 with the NVSHMEM toolkit on the include/link path. It is
45	//    NOT a stub that pretends to work: without the flag it does not exist, and
46	//    any attempt to instantiate the megakernel TP point with it is a loud
47	//    compile error pointing here. Wiring + validating it is the ONE genuinely
48	//    8×H100 task (design §7.5) — swap `LoopbackTransport` → `NvshmemTransport`
49	//    at the call sites and run the §5.4 go/no-go gate.
50	//
51	//  WHY offset-based symmetric addressing (not raw pointers): NVSHMEM's
52	//  symmetric heap guarantees the SAME offset is valid on every PE
53	//  (nvshmem_malloc returns symmetric addresses; nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe) translates
54	//  for NVLink load/store). The loopback reproduces exactly that property with
55	//  base + pe*stride. One addressing model ⇒ one math code path.
56	//
57	//  DETERMINISM (design §5.2, non-negotiable): the fixed-order all-reduce below
58	//  reads every PE's partial in ASCENDING pe order and accumulates fp32. The
59	//  summation order is STRUCTURAL (never timing-dependent), so the result is
60	//  bit-identical on every PE and across reruns — the cross-rank analogue of the
61	//  in-kernel ascending-CTA reduce that made the single-GPU path A/A/A.
62	//  A `nvshmem_float_sum_reduce` collective is deliberately NOT used (its
63	//  reduction order is unspecified) — on NVSHMEM the same ascending-pe loop runs
64	//  over nvshmem_ptr-translated peer pointers (NVLink direct load/store).
65	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66	//
67	// HEADER-ONLY, self-contained: CUDA runtime + the GridBarrier substrate only.
68	// No torch, no NCCL. Compiles for sm_90a with plain nvcc.
69	// ============================================================================

98	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ Xown, const WT* __restrict__ Wshard,

108	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
109	//  LoopbackTransport — single-process symmetric-heap simulation (the 1-GPU
110	//  honest test transport). See the swap-point doc above.
111	//
112	//  Host side: allocate ONE device buffer of `n_pes * stride_floats` floats and
113	//  pass (base, stride_floats, n_pes). Device side: each CTA derives its virtual
114	//  pe from its blockIdx (contiguous CTA groups per PE — `pe_of_cta`).
115	//  The rendezvous is the caller's whole-grid GridBarrier (all virtual PEs share
116	//  the grid), so `rendezvous()` simply forwards to bar.sync().
117	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
118	struct LoopbackTransport {
119	    float*  heap_base;       // [n_pes * stride_floats] device alloc
120	    int64_t stride_floats;   // per-PE symmetric region size
121	    int     n_pes_;          // TP degree being simulated
122	    int     my_pe_;          // this CTA-group's virtual rank
123	
124	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
125	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
126	
127	    // THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset `off`.
128	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
129	        return heap_base + (int64_t)my_pe_ * stride_floats + off;
130	    }
131	    // Peer pe's buffer at the SAME symmetric offset (ascending-pe reads in the

245	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off, float* __restrict__ dst,
246	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
247	    const int P = tr.n_pes();
248	    for (int64_t i = tid; i < n; i += nthreads) {
249	        float acc = 0.0f;
250	        #pragma unroll 1
251	        for (int pe = 0; pe < P; ++pe) {        // ASCENDING pe — fixed order
252	            acc += tr.peer(slot_off, pe)[i];
253	        }
254	        dst[i] = acc;
255	    }
256	}

168	    // each tail reads only its own buffers (opt_components.cuh guarantees unused

170	    float* const m_slice     = state;
171	    float* const v_slice     = state + total;
172	    float* const extra_slice = state + 2 * total;
173	    FusedOptState st;
174	    st.exp_avg    = m_slice;
175	    st.exp_avg_sq = v_slice;
176	    st.ema        = extra_slice;          // grokfast/grokadamw slow-grad EMA
177	    // NeuralGrok psi-net pack (kPsiPackFloats floats at the head of `extra`): the
178	    // cell places [psi_W1 | psi_b1 | psi_W2 | psi_b2] there; bind the device pointers
179	    // so the apply reads real weights (psi_b2 is read on-device from psi_W2[kPsiHidden]).
180	    st.psi_W1     = extra_slice + kPsiW1Off;
181	    st.psi_b1     = extra_slice + kPsiB1Off;
182	    st.psi_W2     = extra_slice + kPsiW2Off;
183	    // PRODIGY (STAGED global-d) state bindings. The cell extends the state buffer
184	    // to [m | v | extra/s_track | loss | param_init | r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] (host
185	    // sizes it to >= 4*total + 4; see dispatch.fused_train_step). The `extra` slice
186	    // doubles as Prodigy's `s` trajectory accumulator (the apply reads st.s_track,
187	    // not st.ema — they alias here, harmless: Prodigy has no slow-grad EMA). The
188	    // trajectory anchor p0 (param_init) follows the loss slot; the 3 persisted
189	    // estimator scalars [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] follow param_init. loss_out points at
190	    // state+3*total (dispatch's loss_slot), so param_init = loss_out + 1.
191	    st.s_track        = extra_slice;            // Prodigy `s` (per-element accumulator)
192	    st.param_init     = loss_out + 1;           // state + 3*total + 1
193	    st.prodigy_persist = loss_out + 1 + total;  // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]
194	    // LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward): sam_dir is the PERSISTENT cached SAM
195	    // direction (g_sam − g), carried across steps in the `extra` slice (aliases the
196	    // grokfast EMA / Prodigy s_track slot — harmless: LookSAM has none of those). The
197	    // in-kernel P2.4 phase WRITES it on SAM steps; the apply tail READS it every step.
198	    st.sam_dir        = extra_slice;            // [total] cached SAM direction
199	    // SuperGrok11/15 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu). State
200	    // layout: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness(total) | phi_pack(4H+1)].
201	    //   * st.mu = the `extra` slice (recomputed each step by the P2.45 precompute; the
202	    //     apply reads it — it aliases sam_dir/ema/s_track, harmless: SG has none).
203	    //   * st.sharpness = loss_slot+1 (PERSISTED (g_sam−g)²; the P2.4 SAM 2nd backward
204	    //     writes it on SAM steps, the cached value is reused on intervening steps).
205	    //   * st.sg_phi_W1/b1/W2 = the phi pack at sharpness+total (host-scattered each step,
206	    //     like NeuralGrok's psi pack); sg_phi_b2 is read on-device from sg_phi_W2[H].
207	    st.mu             = extra_slice;            // [total] meta-net mu (P2.45-filled)
208	    {
209	        float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;       // state + 3*total + 1
210	        float* phi_base   = sharp_base + total; // phi pack after sharpness
211	        st.sharpness = sharp_base;
212	        st.sg_phi_W1 = phi_base + kSgPhiW1Off;
213	        st.sg_phi_b1 = phi_base + kSgPhiB1Off;
214	        st.sg_phi_W2 = phi_base + kSgPhiW2Off;  // sg_phi_b2 read on-device from [H]
215	    }
216	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);   // FULL scalar set (un-frozen bc1/bc2/... + d0/d_coef/beta3 + rho/looksam_sam/sg_rescale)
217	    st.lr = lr;
218	
219	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
220	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
221	    tok.targets   = targets;
222	    tok.B         = B;
223	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
224	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
225	
226	    // Dispatch to the matching kernel instantiation. The fwd+bwd is identical across
227	    // these OptIds; the template differs ONLY in the P3 apply_optimizer<Opt> tail.
228	    // Unsupported opt_ids return cudaErrorInvalidValue → dispatch.cpp throws LOUD (no
229	    // silent scalar/adamw fallback — the no-suppression rule). The STAGED/model-coupled
230	    // optimizers are intentionally NOT cases here (they cannot run as a single launch).
231	    switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id)) {
232	        case OptId::AdamW:
233	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
234	            // TP allow-list (the §1.3/§7.2 explicit-instantiation gate): {1, 8}.
235	            // DP rides in CommCtx at runtime (no Par::kDP read in the kernel), so a
236	            // fixed DP sentinel avoids a DP×TP instantiation matrix (dist_step.md §6.C.4).
237	            if (tp_size == 8) {
238	                using ParTP8 = ::sg::fused::par::ParConfig<
239	                    /*DP=*/8, /*TP=*/8, /*PP=*/1, /*SP=*/1,
240	                    ::sg::fused::par::ZeROStage::Z3>;
241	                // Symmetric TP-slot heap: one publish+reduced slot per CTA-in-PE.
242	                // WORLD-UNIFORM stride (every PE agrees) = ctas_per_pe·2·kTileM·d.
243	                const int P = tp_size;
244	                const int ctas_per_pe = nCTA / P;   // launcher asserts nCTA % P == 0
245	                const int64_t sym_floats =
246	                    ::sg::fused::sm90::tp::tp_heap_stride_floats(ctas_per_pe);
247	                dec_tc_ensure_tp_sym_heap(sc, sym_floats);
248	                ::sg::fused::par::CommCtx comm{};
249	                comm.world_size = 8; comm.tp_size = 8; comm.dp_size = 8;
250	                comm.tp_rank = nvshmem_team_my_pe(/*TP team*/NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD);
251	                comm.tp_sym_heap = sc.tp_sym_heap;
252	                comm.tp_heap_stride_floats = sym_floats;
253	                comm.tp_team_n_pes  = 8;
254	                comm.tp_team_local_pe = comm.tp_rank;
255	                // Store the TP team id as void* (int32 team → intptr → void*); the
256	                // host bootstrap that nvshmem_team_split_strided's the TP group sets
257	                // the real team — NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD for the single-node pure-TP run.
258	                comm.tp_comm_handle = reinterpret_cast<void*>(
259	                    static_cast<intptr_t>(NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD));
260	                return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::AdamW, ParTP8>(
261	                    ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA, comm);
262	            }
263	#endif
264	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::AdamW>(
265	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
266	        case OptId::Lion:
267	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Lion>(
268	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
269	        case OptId::Grokfast:
270	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Grokfast>(
271	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
272	        case OptId::GrokAdamW:
273	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::GrokAdamW>(
274	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
275	        case OptId::NeuralGrok:
276	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::NeuralGrok>(
277	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
278	        case OptId::Prodigy:
279	            // STAGED global-d: the SAME single persistent launch — the d-estimate
280	            // cross-tensor reduction is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.6, between B2 and P3),
281	            // not a separate launch. st carries param_init/prodigy_persist/d0/d_coef/
282	            // beta3; the kernel decays+accumulates the EMA, updates d, applies.
283	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Prodigy>(
284	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
285	        case OptId::Muon:
286	            // STAGED grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME
287	            // single persistent launch — the NS orthogonalization of the 11 2D weights
288	            // (tok/pos/in_proj/out_proj/ff.0/ff.2/out) is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.7,
289	            // between B2/P2.6 and P3), grid-barrier-looped per matrix, NOT a separate
290	            // launch. The per-matrix NS scratch lives in the workspace (dec_tc_muon_floats,
291	            // carved after the Prodigy reduce slots). The persistent momentum buffer is
292	            // the m-slice (st.exp_avg); the 1D/non-2D weights take the AdamW tail in P3
293	            // reading the INDEPENDENT aux_lr/aux_betas (eager Muon adamw_* group). The
294	            // vit twin (mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu) proved this routing.
295	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Muon>(
296	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
297	        case OptId::LookSAM:
298	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME single
299	            // persistent launch — the perturb→2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g is
300	            // an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4, between B2 and P2.5/P3), gated to every-k SAM
301	            // steps by st.looksam_sam. The transient backup + g_sam buffers live in the
302	            // workspace (dec_tc_looksam_floats, carved after the Muon scratch); sam_dir
303	            // persists in the extra slice (st.sam_dir, bound above). The apply tail (P3)
304	            // blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir and runs AdamW. NOT a separate launch.
305	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::LookSAM>(
306	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
307	        case OptId::SuperGrok11:
308	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu/gate (wave-3
309	            // decoder lane): the SAME single persistent launch. The SAM 2nd backward
310	            // (P2.4, sharpness=(g_sam−g)²) + the per-tensor mu precompute (P2.45,
311	            // mu=rescale·phi(g,sharpness)) + the per-tensor cosine gate are ALL
312	            // in-kernel phases between B2 and P3; the apply tail (sg11_sweep_b_step:
313	            // smart_grad=g+(1−gate)·alpha·mu, AdamW) runs in P3. The SAM scratch reuses
314	            // the looksam buffers (dec_tc_looksam_floats); sharpness + the phi pack ride
315	            // the extended state buffer (bound above). NOT a separate launch.
316	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok11>(
317	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
318	        case OptId::SuperGrok15:
319	            // Same SAM 2nd backward + mu precompute as SG11, but SIMPLER tail: the gate
320	            // is a host scalar (st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy)), NO per-tensor cosine stage;
321	            // the apply tail (sg15_sweep_b_step) does the per-coord alpha clip + smart_grad
322	            // = g + gate·a·mu + AdamW. Single persistent launch.
323	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok15>(
324	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
325	        default:
326	            return cudaErrorInvalidValue;  // STAGED/coupled opt not single-launch TC
327	    }
328	}

330	// BACK-COMPAT 17-arg forwarder — the EXACT boundary dispatch.cpp extern-decls and
331	// links today (no tp_size). Forwards to the 18-arg TP-aware definition with
332	// tp_size=1 ⇒ the single-GPU path, byte-identical to the pre-TP launcher. The
333	// shipped _ops symbol is therefore unchanged; the TP path (tp_size>1) is reached
334	// only by a future dispatch.cpp caller of the 18-arg overload (EDIT E.2).
335	cudaError_t mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc(
336	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
337	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
338	        float* state, float* grad, float* workspace_unused, float* loss_out,
339	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets,
340	        float lr, int step, const FusedScalars& scalars, cudaStream_t stream,
341	        int ncta_cap, int opt_id) {
342	    return mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc(
343	        ctx, params, tokens, targets, B, state, grad, workspace_unused, loss_out,
344	        sizes, offsets, lr, step, scalars, stream, ncta_cap, opt_id, /*tp_size=*/1);
345	}
346	
347	// mega_decoder_sg2_tc — the DEDICATED SuperGrok2 TC launcher. SG2 needs the FULL
348	// CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net weight bundle (26 HBM pointers, model-independent) +
349	// per-tensor scalar ARRAYS (alpha/gru_decay/lamb_eff/beta1/bc1/bc2, length P) +
350	// the meta-net state (m/v/mu/slow/gru_state/sharpness), none of which fit the
351	// FusedScalars POD or the generic mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc boundary. So this is
352	// a PARALLEL entry (the generic launcher + the 28 byte-identical cells are
353	// UNTOUCHED). It binds the SG2 state slices, threads the weight bundle + scalar
354	// arrays through FusedOptState's sg2_* fields, and dispatches the OptId::SuperGrok2
355	// kernel instantiation (its P3-SG2 phase runs sg2_meta_stages per tensor: STAGE -1
356	// in-kernel segmented sort → CSA/HCA/GRU/PEER/apply, reading st.sharpness from the
357	// SAM 2nd backward (P2.4, shared with SG11/15)).
358	//
359	// STATE LAYOUT (host sizes it; this carves it):
360	//   [m(total) | v(total) | mu(total) | loss(1) | sharpness(total) | slow(total)
361	//    | gru_state(total*GH)]   ⇒ min_state = (4+1+GH)*total + 1   (GH=gru_hidden=4)
362	// perm/unsort are built IN-KERNEL into the per-CTA workspace (NOT state).
363	cudaError_t mega_decoder_sg2_tc(
364	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
365	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
366	        float* state, float* grad, float* loss_out,
367	        // SG2 meta-net weight bundle (HBM, fp32, model-independent), in SG2Weights order.
368	        const float* input_proj_W, const float* input_proj_b,
369	        const float* csa_q_W, const float* csa_k_W, const float* csa_v_W, const float* csa_out_W,
370	        const float* csa_compress_w, const float* csa_idx_DQ, const float* csa_idx_K,
371	        const float* hca_q_W, const float* hca_k_W, const float* hca_v_W, const float* hca_out_W,
372	        const float* gru_Wz, const float* gru_bz, const float* gru_Wr, const float* gru_br,
373	        const float* gru_Wh, const float* gru_bh,
374	        const float* peer_query_Ws, const float* prod_keys_A, const float* prod_keys_B,
375	        const float* expert_W1, const float* expert_b1, const float* expert_W2, const float* expert_b2,
376	        // per-tensor scalar arrays (device, length kDecNumTensors).
377	        const float* sc_alpha, const float* sc_gru_decay, const float* sc_lamb_eff,
378	        const float* sc_beta1, const float* sc_bc1, const float* sc_bc2,
379	        // shared scalars + the SAM 2nd-backward gate (SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4
380	        // machinery: rho = perturbation radius, sam_on = every-k SAM-step gate).
381	        float rescale, float beta2, float lr, float wd, float eps,
382	        float rho, float sam_on,
383	        int step, cudaStream_t stream, int ncta_cap) {
384	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
385	    // gru_state spans total*GH (GH=DecSG2Dims::gru_hidden); the layout is fixed by
386	    // the kernel's SG2State carve, so the slices below need no GH arithmetic here.
387	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
388	
389	    int dev = 0;
390	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
391	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
392	    int n_sms = 1;
393	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
394	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
395	    int nCTA = n_sms;
396	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
397	
398	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
399	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
400	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
401	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
402	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
403	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;
404	
405	    // Bind the SG2 state slices: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness | slow | gru_state].
406	    FusedOptState st;
407	    st.exp_avg     = state;                       // m
408	    st.exp_avg_sq  = state + total;               // v
409	    st.mu          = state + 2 * total;           // expert-output EMA
410	    // loss_out points at state + 3*total (dispatch's loss slot).
411	    float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;             // state + 3*total + 1
412	    st.sharpness   = sharp_base;                  // (g_sam − g)² (SAM 2nd backward, P2.4)
413	    st.sg2_slow    = sharp_base + total;          // grokfast slow-grad EMA
414	    st.sg2_gru_state = st.sg2_slow + total;       // [total*GH] per-element GRU state
415	    // meta-net weight bundle (HBM).
416	    st.sg2_input_proj_W = input_proj_W; st.sg2_input_proj_b = input_proj_b;
417	    st.sg2_csa_q_W = csa_q_W; st.sg2_csa_k_W = csa_k_W; st.sg2_csa_v_W = csa_v_W;
418	    st.sg2_csa_out_W = csa_out_W; st.sg2_csa_compress_w = csa_compress_w;
419	    st.sg2_csa_idx_DQ = csa_idx_DQ; st.sg2_csa_idx_K = csa_idx_K;
420	    st.sg2_hca_q_W = hca_q_W; st.sg2_hca_k_W = hca_k_W; st.sg2_hca_v_W = hca_v_W;
421	    st.sg2_hca_out_W = hca_out_W;
422	    st.sg2_gru_Wz = gru_Wz; st.sg2_gru_bz = gru_bz; st.sg2_gru_Wr = gru_Wr;
423	    st.sg2_gru_br = gru_br; st.sg2_gru_Wh = gru_Wh; st.sg2_gru_bh = gru_bh;
424	    st.sg2_peer_query_Ws = peer_query_Ws; st.sg2_prod_keys_A = prod_keys_A;
425	    st.sg2_prod_keys_B = prod_keys_B;
426	    st.sg2_expert_W1 = expert_W1; st.sg2_expert_b1 = expert_b1;
427	    st.sg2_expert_W2 = expert_W2; st.sg2_expert_b2 = expert_b2;
428	    // per-tensor scalar arrays.
429	    st.sg2_alpha = sc_alpha; st.sg2_gru_decay = sc_gru_decay; st.sg2_lamb_eff = sc_lamb_eff;
430	    st.sg2_beta1 = sc_beta1; st.sg2_bc1 = sc_bc1; st.sg2_bc2 = sc_bc2;
431	    st.sg2_rescale = rescale;
432	    // shared scalars the SG2 phase reads (beta2/lr/wd/eps via FusedScalars fields).
433	    st.beta2 = beta2; st.lr = lr; st.wd = wd; st.eps = eps;
434	    // SAM 2nd-backward gate: SG2 reuses the LookSAM P2.4 machinery. st.rho is the
435	    // perturbation radius (SG2's sam_rho); st.looksam_sam is the every-k SAM-step gate
436	    // (1.0 ⇒ run the in-kernel perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sharpness=(g_sam−g)² this step;
437	    // 0.0 ⇒ reuse the cached sharpness). On a non-SAM step the cached sharpness feeds
438	    // the meta-net verbatim (eager-faithful).
439	    st.rho = rho;
440	    st.looksam_sam = sam_on;
441	
442	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
443	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
444	    tok.targets   = targets;
445	    tok.B         = B;
446	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
447	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
448	
449	    return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok2>(
450	        ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
451	}
452	
453	}}}  // namespace sg::fused::sm90

1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_LAYER_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_LAYER_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/tp_layer.cuh — TENSOR-PARALLEL math for the L3-TC decoder
5	// megakernel: the Megatron column/row split geometry, the sharded wgmma tile
6	// GEMMs, and the two in-step all-reduce points.
7	//
8	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §5.1 (where the all-reduce
9	// lands — col-parallel in_proj/ff0, row-parallel out_proj/ff2, TWO all-reduces
10	// per layer) + §5.2 (fixed-order in-kernel reduce, via tp_transport.cuh).
11	// Authored 1-GPU per design §7 (task #25 phase-2, Lane C). The TP MATH here is
12	// the durable deliverable; the transport behind it is the swap point
13	// (tp_transport.cuh — loopback now, NVSHMEM at the 8× window).
14	//
15	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
16	//  THE MEGATRON SPLIT ON THIS KERNEL'S WEIGHT LAYOUT (all row-major [Nout,Kin],
17	//  matching DecWeights / decoder_layout.cuh):
18	//
19	//   weight (tidx)        split          rank r owns                 comm
20	//   ------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	//   in_proj  (2,14)      COLUMN(QKV)    rows {q,k,v}×[r·d/P,(r+1)·d/P)   none (fwd)
22	//   in_proj_b(3,15)      COLUMN(QKV)    same 3-block rows                none
23	//   out_proj (4,16)      ROW            cols [r·d/P,(r+1)·d/P)       fwd all-reduce ①
24	//   out_b    (5,17)      REPLICATED     (added after reduce ①, identical on all)
25	//   ff.0     (10,22)     COLUMN         rows [r·dff/P,(r+1)·dff/P)       none (fwd)
26	//   ff.0_b   (11,23)     COLUMN         same rows                        none
27	//   ff.2     (12,24)     ROW            cols [r·dff/P,(r+1)·dff/P)   fwd all-reduce ②
28	//   ff.2_b   (13,25)     REPLICATED     (added after reduce ②)
29	//   tok/pos  (0,1)       REPLICATED     —                                 none*
30	//   LN γ/β   (6..9,18..21,26,27) REPLICATED (LN runs on full-width, post-reduce)
31	//   head w/b (28,29)     REPLICATED     (V=99 — vocab-parallel head is the
32	//                                        documented future extension, not built)
33	//
34	//   * replicated tensors receive BIT-IDENTICAL grads on every TP rank: their
35	//     producing adjoints sit downstream of fixed-order all-reduces (dh0 is the
36	//     reduced in_proj dX; LN/head inputs are full-width post-reduce activations)
37	//     — so no grad comm is needed for them and determinism is structural.
38	//
39	//  THE QKV 3-BLOCK SHARD: in_proj packs [q(d)|k(d)|v(d)] along Nout=3d, heads
40	//  inside each block. Rank r owns heads [r·H/P,(r+1)·H/P) ⇒ for EACH of q,k,v
41	//  the row range [r·d/P,(r+1)·d/P). The rank's DENSE shard buffer is the three
42	//  blocks concatenated: [q_own | k_own | v_own], 3·d/P rows of Kin=d — so the

148	// Contiguous own-range along a split extent. Requires P | extent (TP degrees
149	// are powers of two and d/dff/3d at every ladder width are multiples of 8·64;

151	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ void tp_own_range(
152	        int extent, int P, int r, int* lo, int* hi) {
153	    const int per = extent / P;     // caller asserts extent % P == 0
154	    *lo = r * per;
155	    *hi = *lo + per;

165	//  Host-side dense shard packing maps (how a rank STORES its shard). The rank
166	//  keeps its shard DENSE — [Nout/P, Kin] for Col, [Nout, Kin/P] for Row, and
167	//  for ColQKV the q|k|v own-blocks concatenated [3·d/P, d] — so every sharded
168	//  GEMM below reads it exactly like the unsharded kernel reads a full weight
169	//  (row-major, no strides). These index helpers define the pack ONCE (host
170	//  packers + tests both call them; no duplicated arithmetic).
171	//    Col   : dense row i  ↔ full row (own_lo + i)
172	//    Row   : dense col j  ↔ full col (own_lo + j)
173	//    ColQKV: dense row i  ↔ full row (block(i)·d + own_lo + i % (d/P)),
174	//            block(i) = i / (d/P) ∈ {0,1,2} = {q,k,v}
175	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
176	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int tp_col_full_row(int own_lo, int i) {
177	    return own_lo + i;
178	}
179	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int tp_row_full_col(int own_lo, int j) {
180	    return own_lo + j;
181	}
182	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int tp_colqkv_full_row(int d, int P, int r, int i) {
183	    const int per = d / P;          // rows per (q|k|v) block on one rank
184	    const int blk = i / per;        // 0=q, 1=k, 2=v
185	    const int off = i % per;
186	    return blk * d + r * per + off;
187	}
